text:
Someone else pushed commits to `origin/main` after you last fetched, so your local `main` isn't a descendant of the remote tip — Git refuses the non-fast-forward push rather than dropping their work.

Fix:

1. `git fetch origin` — get the remote commits.
2. Integrate. Pick one:
   - `git rebase origin/main` — replays your local commits on top; keeps history linear. Preferred if your commits aren't pushed/shared anywhere yet.
   - `git merge origin/main` — creates a merge commit; safer if others have already based work on your commits.
3. Resolve conflicts if any (`git status` lists them; `git rebase --continue` or commit the merge).
4. `git push`.

Shortcut for the common case: `git pull --rebase` does steps 1–2 in one go.

Don't use `git push --force` here — it would delete the remote commits you don't have. If you ever do need to overwrite, `--force-with-lease` at least fails when the remote moved unexpectedly.
